claims.text: - **The money**: $47 million raised in total, most recently $30 million at a $500 million valuation announced 2026-04-24, led by Craft.[^1]

The company's GlobeNewswire release disagrees with its own blog twice on the same day: the release subheadline says "50K daily downloads" where the blog says "150,000+ daily downloads" — a 3x gap — and the release reports total funding of $48 million against the blog's $47 million.[^2] [^1]
The official Comfy Registry API reports a `total` of 4,993 published node packs as of 2026-08-05, roughly one-twelfth of the advertised "60,000+ nodes."[^9]

The bot's PR-comment template tells contributors the CLA "would enable us to relicense the project under a more permissive license in the future, giving the project and its community greater flexibility" — framed as the most important benefit.[^21]
Everything is now in natural language. No nodes, no download, no GPU, no node graphs if you don't want them.

Credit prices reproduce the underlying providers' public list prices to the cent — Google Veo 3.1 with audio bills at 84.4 credits/sec, or $0.40/sec, Google's list price; GPT-5 bills at 263.75 credits per million tokens, or $1.25/1M, OpenAI's list price — and the docs state "Actual usage from the API is authoritative."[^16]

As of 2026-08-05 the published tiers run Standard $20/month for 4,200 credits, Creator $35 for 7,400, Pro $100 for 21,100 and Team $700 for 147,700, with an unpriced Enterprise tier and annual pricing at $16/$28/$80/$630 per month

AUTOMATIC1111's stable-diffusion-webui carries 164,387 stars and 30,545 forks, more than ComfyUI on both counts — while its `master` branch has received no commit since 2024-07-27, and its final release v1.10.1 points at that same July 2024 commit.[^7] [^8]

The CHORD nodes ship under the Ubisoft Machine Learning License, research-only, with commercial use strictly prohibited — and Ubisoft's own La Forge blog says the results are "not production-ready yet, but a solid first step," and that "the quality isn't where it needs to be for AAA video games material."[^39] [^40]

First, licensing: FLUX.1 [dev] version 1.1.1 permits commercial use of outputs in section 2(d) while conditioning the entire grant in section 1(c) on receiving no direct or indirect payment — so the default local FLUX workflow is a gray zone for revenue-generating work.[^64]
On 2025-05-01 the Department of Justice announced that Ryan Mitchell Kramer of Santa Clarita, a/k/a NullBulge, agreed to plead guilty to two counts
Meanwhile EU AI Act Article 50 transparency obligations became applicable on 2026-08-02, and deployers cannot discharge their disclosure duty by relying on a provider's marking.[^66]

Applying the same unit to compute: 0.27 credits/sec for the RTX PRO 6000 is 972 credits/hour, or about $4.61 per GPU-hour, against roughly $1.07/hour for the same card on Vast.ai and a market median on-demand price near $2.20/hour as of 2026-08-05.[^15] [^78]
Comfy Cloud MCP shipped in public beta on metered GPUs; Comfy Local MCP is in private test and not publicly available; the in-app agent is private alpha, waitlist-only.[^19]

The comparison set is itself thinning — Invoke's hosted platform shut down when its founding team joined Adobe, and invoke.ai now publishes no pricing tiers at all, so its 27,767 stars measure a historical position rather than a live one.[^56] [^7]
The one exception is OpenRouter, priced roughly 2.4x the equivalent direct-API rows.[^16]
The repository's root commit is `220afe3`, and GitHub records the project as created at 2023-01-17T03:15:56Z.[^6]
An independent audit of all eleven found genuine artifacts naming ComfyUI for four of them and nothing at all for HP, Harman and Lucid
